questions.def: Past continuous reports a continuous action in the past.
questions.question: She said she ___ to the party, but I didn't believe her.

questions.def: "Tell" takes an object pronoun, unlike "said".
questions.question: He ___ me he would be late.

questions.def: "Deny" is followed by a gerund (-ing form).
questions.question: He ___ breaking the vase.

questions.def: "Claimed" implies a statement made without proof.
questions.question: They ___ they had finished the project early.

questions.def: "Whether" is more formal than "if" in reported questions.
questions.question: He asked me ___ I liked coffee.

questions.def: We don't use an object pronoun directly after 'said'.
questions.question: She said me that she was tired yesterday.

questions.def: "Warned" + object pronoun + infinitive is correct structure.
questions.question: She ___ me not to go there alone.

questions.def: "Reported" is the standard verb for news reporting.
questions.question: The news ___ that the prime minister had resigned.

questions.def: "Agreed" implies consent to a request or suggestion.
questions.question: He ___ to help me with the report.

questions.def: "Reminded" + object pronoun + infinitive is correct.
questions.question: She ___ me to call my mother.

questions.def: "Ordered" implies authority and a command.
questions.question: The teacher ___ the students to be quiet.

questions.def: "Will" changes to "would" in reported speech.
questions.question: She said she ___ be there by six.

questions.def: "Advised" + object pronoun + infinitive is correct.
questions.question: My doctor ___ me to exercise more.

questions.def: "Insisted" implies a firm declaration of belief.
questions.question: He ___ that he was innocent.

questions.def: "If" introduces a yes/no question in reported speech.
questions.question: She asked me ___ I had ever been to Italy.

questions.def: "Explained" introduces a detailed account.
questions.question: She ___ that the process was complicated.

questions.def: "Recalled" implies remembering something specifically.
questions.question: The witness ___ seeing the accident.

questions.def: "Implied" means suggesting something without stating it.
questions.question: He ___ he could help us.

questions.def: "Complained" expresses dissatisfaction or annoyance.
questions.question: He ___ that the service was slow.

questions.def: "Refused" implies a denial of a request or demand.
questions.question: The suspect ___ to cooperate with the police.

questions.def: Reported questions follow statement word order.
questions.question: He asked me what ___ doing.

questions.def: Use the subjunctive after 'recommend'.
questions.question: The doctor recommended that he ___ to a specialist.

questions.def: "Assured" implies a promise or guarantee.
questions.question: He ___ me that he'd call me back later.

questions.def: "Have/has" changes to "had" in reported speech.
questions.question: She said she ___ finished the report by then.

questions.def: Use 'would' to report future tense in the past.
questions.question: He said he ___ me the book the next day.

questions.def: 'Admitted' implies acknowledging something negative.
questions.question: They ___ they were going to be late.

questions.def: Use the past simple to report a past question.
questions.question: He ___ if I had finished the report.

questions.def: Use past perfect continuous for past actions reported in past.
questions.question: She explained that she ___ working there for five years.

questions.def: 'Mentioned' often takes a gerund (verb+ing).
questions.question: The manager mentioned ___ a pay raise soon.

questions.def: 'Deny' is followed by a gerund, and needs past tense.
questions.question: He ___ stealing the money.
